thread:
Maya (runtime): Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC. Ran the canary across A100/H100/L4 pools and hit a surprising slow path on L4 for long-context (seq_len ~4096). Pasting minimal logs and probe output below.

Alex (arch): deferring to your logs — curious if this is probe-detection or a downstream kernel mismatch.

Maya (runtime): Logs:
```
[2025-11-04T14:02:10Z] device=/dev/nvidia0 probe_result={
  "device_type": "L4",
  "supports_warp_shuffle_32": true,
  "supports_warp_shuffle_64": false,
  "tensor_core_bf16": false,
  "max_shared_mem_kb": 96
}
[2025-11-04T14:02:11Z] selected_kernel=attention_generic_v2 (fallback) latency=12.3ms
[2025-11-04T14:02:11Z] selected_kernel=attention_a100_opt latency=9.1ms (not used - capability mismatch)
```

Tess (eng infra): OK — so the runtime probe is reporting warp_shuffle_64=false which prevents using our warp-optimized kernels. L4 appears to have smaller shared memory and fewer TC features; that explains fallback.

Ryan (perf): Can we get a microbenchmark that isolates shuffle vs shared-mem pressure? The delta between generic and a100_opt is large at long seqs. If we can prove the hot path is shuffle-limited we can prioritize a lighter-weight L4-specialized kernel rather than generic.

Deepa (mlops): FYI, customer workload (chat history + retrieval) hits 4k tokens often. If L4 is pinned as generic we get ~25% cost increase. We should try to avoid generic for L4 where possible.

Alex (arch): Proposal: two-layer gating model. 1) Static probe at node boot that reports capability bitset (warp_shuffle_64, shuffle64_atomic, tc_bf16, max_sm_mem) 2) Dynamic runtime probe that samples a short synthetic across seq_len buckets (512/1024/2048/4096) on first warmup and records which kernels hit PTX+SM instructions without bank conflicts.

Maya (runtime): Implementation detail: store capability bitset in node metadata and in the kernel registry add "min_capability_mask" per kernel. At runtime prefer exact-match kernel, then best-fit (smallest missing features), then generic fallback. Also allow an override with env var RDW_FORCE_KERNEL=... for debugging.

Tess (eng infra): Sounds good. A couple of tradeoffs: static-only gating is fast but brittle (driver/firmware updates can change behavior). Dynamic probes add a small warmup cost and must run with conservative timeouts. We should run probes asynchronously and mark node as "probed" when complete so requests can still route.

Ryan (perf): For rollout, propose: internal canary (10% traffic) -> perf-ci stress (long seqs) -> expand to 50% with observability flags (per-kernel counters + tail-latency SLO alarms). perf-ci I can add tests to assert token-per-ms and 99.9th latency doesn't regress. @perf-ci please schedule.

perf-ci: added a perf suite item: attention-kernel-selection-l4-longseq. Running on canary pool. Results ETA: 48h.

Deepa (mlops): We should also consider a small L4-optimized kernel that does not require warp_shuffle_64 but uses cooperative shared-memory tiling and fp16 math to get most of the benefit. That will be smaller dev effort than full generic rewrite.

Alex (arch): Agree. Prioritization: 1) gating infra + kernel registry changes (runtime) 2) small L4-optimized kernel (arch + perf) 3) dynamic synthetic probes (infra + runtime) 4) metrics/rollout wiring (observability).

Maya (runtime): I'll open the runtime PR to add node probe metadata and registry matching. Plan: probe runs at startup -> writes /var/lib/rdw/probe.json -> runtime falls back to async probe if missing. Also add RDW_FORCE_KERNEL override.

Tess (eng infra): I'll add the systemd unit change and canary label for nodes so we can target the canary fleet. Also add a flag to avoid probing on very short-lived instances.

Alex (arch): I'll draft the L4 kernel plan. Quick note about correctness: we must run the full fp16/bf16 numerics smoke tests and the KV-cache consistency suite. I'll add those to the kernel CI matrix.

Ryan (perf): For alerts, we'll track per-kernel p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. If fallback rate > 15% or tail latency regresses >10% we'll rollback the canary.

Maya (runtime): A couple of edge cases: multi-GPU pinned jobs where one GPU reports capabilities and another doesn't. Runtime should require per-device capability checks and enforce kernel selection per-device slice. We'll add guards to avoid cross-device kernel dispatch.

Alex (arch): Good catch. Also need to update compilation pipeline: keep precompiled kernel artifacts for A100/H100/L4 to avoid JIT on first run. That shortens the warmup impact.

Deepa (mlops): Can we capture a small golden prompt set and run automatic output diff to ensure numerical parity across kernels? Even small ops reorder can change rounding and downstream ranking. We'll add a regression threshold.

Maya (runtime): Yes — adding deterministic eval harness. If diff > 0.2% flagged as quality regression.

Tess (eng infra): Ownership:
- Maya: runtime probe + registry matching (PR in 3 days)
- Alex: L4 kernel design doc + CI matrix updates (EOW)
- Ryan: perf tests + alerting rules (48h)
- Deepa: eval harness + golden prompt set (EOW)

Maya (runtime): Will also add a small telemetry event: rdw.kernel.selection {device_type, selected_kernel, fallback_reason} so we can monitor in prod. Keep payload tiny.

Alex (arch): One more thought — we should differentiate two types of capability flags: functional (correctness required) and performance (optional). Keep kernel registry to mark which are "perf-only" so runtime can decide to use perf kernels only when SLOs permit.

Ryan (perf): Agreed. That's important for graceful degradation.

Maya (runtime): Ok that's the plan. I'll kick off the runtime PR and tag you all. Thanks. :thumbsup:
